title: Detroit's local musicians and bands
summary: They name musicians from Detroit such as Billy Boyd, Don Redman and Sidney De Paris, and later Milt Jackson and Kenny Burrell.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Were there any interesting local musicians in Detroit... Detroit at that time was really not noted. Later on it became noted as a-----

Well, you had guys like Lanky Bowman and you had Billy Boyd, you know, the guy that's calling me every day. Billy come from Detroit and then he went with McKinney's Cotton Pickers. I think he was the youngest conductor they ever had. McKinney had a good band. Fathead and De Paris...that De Paris boy I think was with him. Not Wilborn* but the other one.
Sidney. And Don Redman come from Detroit. Don was

well known, you know, as a writer and as a playing musician. Strange as it may seem, you know there are not that many original, like. In Kansas City you had Thamon Hayes and start naming off a whole slew of musicians that came from there.
Yeah, it wasn't, I guess, until after the War there were a lot of guys came out of Detroit like Milt Jackson and Kenny Burrell and...
And they were the fore...they were not the forerunners, they were the aftermath of the exodus, shall we say.
